Since 2026.8.9, mise prefers a release's `.tar.zst` asset over `.tar.xz`. For LLVM, that broke installs:

```
$ mise use -g github:llvm/llvm-project
Error: Failed to install github:llvm/llvm-project@latest: failed to extract tar: …/LLVM-23.1.2-Linux-X64.tar.zst to …: Frame requires too much memory for decoding
```

LLVM compresses its `.tar.zst` releases with a 1 GiB window (`zstd --long=30`
items.title: fix(install): extract .tar.zst archives compressed with a long window

## Summary

Ports jdx/aube's `benchmarks/pgo.bash` three-phase PGO pipeline to mise, wired into the release tarball builds. Follow-up to #11025 / #11027 / #11029 — this attacks the remaining first-touch page-in cost with profile-guided code layout, the last lever identified in that series.

- **`scripts/pgo.bash`** — instrument (`-Cprofile-generate`) → train → rebuild (`-Cprofile-use`). Training is hermetic and offline: throwaway HOME + isolated `MISE_*_DIR`s exercising settings/config load, too
items.title: perf(release): add PGO builds for natively-trainable release targets

Description
With global:
[settings]
java.shorthand_vendor = "corretto"
and a project containing:
[tools]
java = "21"
mise correctly resolves 21 to the latest Corretto 21 release, but does not recognize an already-installed vendor-qualified JDK of that exact version.
For example, corretto-21.0.12.9.1 is installed, but mise still reports 21.0.12.9.1 as missing.
This is not the same as #8170, which has been closed.
